headline: Linux creator Linus Torvalds is working on a hefty improvement to the Linux kernel with Anthropic's Claude Code AI coding tool, Phoronix reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: only the headline could be checked, from a single outlet, so the nature and size of the improvement are unverified.
importance_line: Linux developers and maintainers are affected first, then the many organisations that run Linux; it comes days after Torvalds told Open Source Summit Europe, as ZDNET reported on 9 Oct 2026, "I actually really like using AI" while saying it is also stressing maintainers out, but what the improvement is and how much Claude Code wrote are not known.
summary: Phoronix reports that Linus Torvalds, who created and leads the development of the Linux kernel (the core of the Linux operating system), is working on a hefty kernel improvement with Anthropic's Claude Code, its AI coding tool.
notes: Phoronix blocked (HTTP 403); no other outlet found for this specific story. ZDNET (9 Oct 2026) and XDA (11 Oct 2026) cover Torvalds's separate 'really likes using AI' remarks, which are context, not this story.
